# Stepper

Figma: [06h. Stepper](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-938) · Family: 06 Navigation · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-15

Shows progress through a multi-step flow and where the user is in it. Built from two atoms - StepIndicator and StepConnector - into horizontal and vertical layouts across LTR + RTL.

### StepIndicator

28px step circle of a Stepper: check when completed, brand number when current, outlined number when upcoming, error fill with ! when the step failed.

Level: atom · Part of: Stepper

Use when:
- Inside Stepper; set Number and State per step

Don't use when:
- Timelines of deal events: use TimelineNode
- Counts on icons: use Badge Count

Accessibility: State must be announced in text (completed, current, error), not only by colour or icon.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Number | `number` | text |  | 1 |
| State | `state` | variant | completed, current, upcoming, error | completed |

### StepConnector

Line between step indicators, brand when complete and muted when incomplete, horizontal or vertical, stretching to fill the gap.

Level: atom · Part of: Stepper

Use when:
- Inside Stepper between StepIndicators; the connector before the current step is complete

Don't use when:
- Visual separators: use Divider
- Progress amounts: use ProgressBar

Accessibility: Decorative; hide from assistive tech.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orientation | `orientation` | variant | horizontal, vertical | horizontal |
| State | `state` | variant | complete, incomplete | complete |

### Stepper

Process stepper that shows an ordered multi-step flow (Account, Identity, Bank details, Review) with completed, current and upcoming steps. It shows progress through a task; it is not a numeric input.

Level: organism · Contains: StepIndicator, StepConnector

Use when:
- Onboarding, KYC, guided investment or checkout flows with 3 to 5 ordered steps
- Showing total length and progress up front (Orientation=horizontal on wide layouts)
- Long labels or narrow columns (Orientation=vertical)

Don't use when:
- Incrementing a quantity with minus and plus: use NumericStepper
- Hierarchy or location: use Breadcrumb
- Safqah KYC checklist screens: use KYCStep
- A single short form: no stepper

Accessibility: Ordered list with the current step marked aria-current=step; progress also stated in text (Step 2 of 4); progress flows right to left in RTL.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orientation | `orientation` | variant | horizontal, vertical | horizontal |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

A Stepper breaks a long task into a clear, ordered sequence and shows where the user is, what is done, and what is left. It reduces the cognitive load of a big form and gives a sense of progress.

### When to use

- A multi-step flow with a clear order - KYC, onboarding, a guided investment, checkout.
- When the user benefits from seeing total length and progress up front.

### When not to use

- A single short form - just show the form.
- For hierarchy or location, not sequence - use a Breadcrumb (06f).

### Live preview

### Atomic architecture

Two atoms alternate to form the rail; the organism arranges them with labels in either orientation.

### Atoms

- StepIndicator - the 28px circle. completed (check, brand fill), current (number, brand fill), upcoming (number, outlined muted). Number prop.
- StepConnector - the line between indicators. complete (brand) or incomplete (muted), horizontal or vertical; stretches to fill the gap.

### Organism

- Stepper - Indicator / Connector / … with a label per step. Orientation horizontal · vertical × Direction.

> **Info:** Exactly one step is current; every step before it is completed, every step after is upcoming. The connector before the current step is complete; the rest are incomplete.

### Anatomy

- Indicator - a numbered circle that becomes a checkmark once the step is completed.
- Label - the step name; muted while upcoming, solid once reached.
- Connector - the line joining indicators; fills with brand colour as steps complete.
- Current marker - the single in-progress step the rest of the page is about.

### States

Each step indicator is in one of three states.

completed

current

upcoming

error

- completed - brand fill + checkmark; the step is done (and usually editable by going back).
- current - brand fill + number; the active step the user is on now.
- upcoming - outlined + muted number; not yet reached and not interactive.
- error - error fill + “!”; the step failed validation. Block advancing until it’s resolved.

### Orientation

Same flow, two directions of travel.

horizontal

Steps left-to-right with labels below. For wide layouts and short flows (≤ ~5 steps).

vertical

Steps top-to-bottom with labels beside. For narrow columns, sidebars, and flows with longer labels or descriptions.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Progress flows with the reading direction - left-to-right in LTR, right-to-left in RTL.

LTR

Step 1 on the left; the completed fill grows rightward.

RTL

Step 1 on the right; the rail mirrors; Arabic labels.

### Behavior

- Exactly one current step; everything before it is completed, everything after is upcoming.
- Linear - the user advances one step at a time and can step back to edit a completed step.
- Non-linear (optional) - completed steps become tappable so the user can jump back directly.
- If a step fails validation, surface an error state on its indicator and block advancing.
- Keep it to ~3–5 steps; for more, group them or move to a full multi-page flow.

### Code examples

### HTML · ARIA

```dart
<ol class="stepper" aria-label="KYC progress">
  <li class="step done"><a href="#account">Account</a></li>
  <li class="step current" aria-current="step">Identity</li>
  <li class="step upcoming"><span aria-disabled="true">Bank details</span></li>
  <li class="step upcoming"><span aria-disabled="true">Review</span></li>
</ol>
<!-- connectors are drawn with CSS, not real list items -->
```

### Usage - Do and Don’t

Do

Do mark one current step, complete earlier ones, and let users step back to edit.

Don’t

Don’t cram many steps into a horizontal rail - keep ~3–5; go vertical or split for more.

Do

Do use the vertical layout when labels are long or the flow lives in a narrow column.

Don’t

Don’t use a stepper for hierarchy or free navigation - that’s a Breadcrumb or a TabBar.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Two atoms - StepIndicator and StepConnector - compose both orientations. The completed checkmark is a drawn vector; the connector stretches via layoutGrow to fill the gap.

> **Info:** To build a flow: set step 1..n−1 to completed, step n (current) to current, the rest upcoming; set the connector before the current step to complete.

> **Warning:** An error state (State=error) is available - error fill + “!” - for steps that fail validation; pair it with an inline error message and block advancing.
